title: A quasi-coherent module on a qcqs scheme is a directed colimit of modules of finite presentation (Stacks 01PK)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. An $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ is *of finite presentation* if every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U\to0$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules (Stacks, Modules, Definition 01BN). Then there exist a directed set $I$ (a nonempty preordered set in which any two elements have a common upper bound), a system $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i}:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules of finite presentation over $I$ ($\varphi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi_{i''i'}\circ\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_{i''i}$), and $\mathcal O_X$-module maps $\varphi_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F$ with $\varphi_{i'}\circ\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_i$, such that $(\mathcal F,(\varphi_i))$ is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the system in the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PK (lemma-directed-colimit-finite-presentation, line 3193; proof via Lemma lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation and Categories, Lemma 0032 lemma-directed-category-system)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the filtered diagram).* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-filtered-colimit-finite-presentation] (Properties 01PJ; $X$ is qcqs and $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent) there are a small filtered category $\mathcal I$, a functor $M:\mathcal I\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ with every $M(x)$ of finite presentation, and maps $\varphi_x:M(x)\to\mathcal F$ with $\varphi_y\circ M(a)=\varphi_x$ for $a:x\to y$, such that $(\mathcal F,(\varphi_x)_x)$ is a colimit of $M$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PK (lemma-directed-colimit-finite-presentation, line 3193), proof (line 3215): 'direct consequence of Lemma 01PJ and Categories, Lemma 0032'

proof.text: *Step 2 (dualize).* The opposite category $\mathcal I^{\rm op}$ is small and cofiltered (the three conditions of filteredness for $\mathcal I$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] read in $\mathcal I^{\rm op}$ are the three conditions of cofilteredness: nonempty, any two objects receive morphisms from a common object, any two parallel morphisms are equalized on the source side). Let $\mathcal C=\Mod(\mathcal O_X)^{\rm op}$ and $D=M^{\rm op}:\mathcal I^{\rm op}\to\mathcal C$. A family $g_x:T\to D(x)$ in $\mathcal C$ with $D(a)\circ g_x=g_y$ is a family $M(x)\to T$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ compatible with the $M(a)$, so the colimit property of $(\mathcal F,(\varphi_x))$ (Step 1) says exactly that $(\mathcal F,(\varphi_x^{\rm op}:\mathcal F\to D(x))_x)$ is a limit cone of $D$ in $\mathcal C$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] (a limit in $\mathcal C$ is a colimit in $\mathcal C^{\rm op}=\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$). This is the definition read in the opposite category.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PK (lemma-directed-colimit-finite-presentation, line 3193), proof (line 3215): 'direct consequence of Lemma 01PJ and Categories, Lemma 0032'

proof.text: *Step 3 (reindex by a directed set: Categories 0032).* By [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] (Categories, Lemma 0032, Mathlib `IsFiltered.exists_directed` with `Functor.Final`; applied to the small cofiltered category $\mathcal I^{\rm op}$, the category $\mathcal C=\Mod(\mathcal O_X)^{\rm op}$, $D=M^{\rm op}$ and the limit cone of Step 2) there are a nonempty directed set $(A,\le)$, objects $x_a$ of $\mathcal I$ ($a\in A$) and morphisms $x_b\to x_a$ of $\mathcal I^{\rm op}$, i.e. morphisms $\psi_{ba}:x_a\to x_b$ of $\mathcal I$ ($a\le b$), with $\psi_{aa}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\psi_{cb}\circ\psi_{ba}=\psi_{ca}$ ($a\le b\le c$), such that $(\mathcal F,(\varphi_{x_a}^{\rm op})_{a\in A})$ is a limit in $\mathcal C$ of the inverse system $(D(x_a),D(\psi_{ba}^{\rm op}))$; read back in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ as in Step 2, $(\mathcal F,(\varphi_{x_a})_{a\in A})$ is a colimit of the system $(M(x_a),M(\psi_{ba}))_{a\le b}$ over $A$. (Stacks also invokes the existence of colimits in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$; it is not needed here, since the cited lemma transfers the colimit property itself, Mathlib `Functor.Final.isColimitWhiskerEquiv`.)

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PK (lemma-directed-colimit-finite-presentation, line 3193), proof (line 3215): 'direct consequence of Lemma 01PJ and Categories, Lemma 0032'

proof.text: *Step 4 (conclusion).* Put $I=A$, $\mathcal F_a=M(x_a)$, $\varphi_{ba}=M(\psi_{ba})$ for $a\le b$, and $\varphi_a=\varphi_{x_a}$. Each $\mathcal F_a$ is of finite presentation (Step 1); $\varphi_{aa}=M(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ and $\varphi_{cb}\varphi_{ba}=M(\psi_{cb}\psi_{ba})=\varphi_{ca}$ by functoriality of $M$; $\varphi_b\circ\varphi_{ba}=\varphi_{x_b}\circ M(\psi_{ba})=\varphi_{x_a}=\varphi_a$ by the cocone property of Step 1; and $(\mathcal F,(\varphi_a))$ is a colimit of the system [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] by Step 3. This is the statement.
